statement.summary: Lemma A.1 is frozen as two Props: the sandwich 0 ≤ q^m(p^{-j}) ≤ σ^{N_j} is `lemA1SandwichStatement`, the union bound at j = 1 is `lemA1UnionBoundStatement`; `lemA1Statement` is their conjunction. q^m(c) is the literal real-valued truncation `qTrunc` (real power `Real.rpow` with exponent c·n^d·∏ p_i^{-v_i}), p = p_{m+1} is `primeAt n m` (0-indexed increasing list of prime factors), N_j is the real number `Nj n d p j = n^d/p^j`. The title's 'union interpretation' (q^m(p^{−j}) counts the configurations of T_j fixed by some order-p_i subgroup) is a step of the proof, frozen as the auxiliary `unionInterpretationStatement`; it is not part of the lemma's statement.
deltas: p_1 < … < p_k is `primeAt n 0 < … < primeAt n (k-1)` (0-indexed); the appendix's p := p_{m+1} is `primeAt n m`; Σ_{i ≤ m} is Σ_{i ∈ range m}.
q^m(c) is `qTrunc n d σ m c : ℝ`, with v ∈ {0,…,d}^m as `v : Fin m → Fin (d+1)`, the power of σ as `Real.rpow` with real exponent c·n^d·∏ p_i^{-v_i} (zpow), no rounding.
p^{-j} is the real zpow `(primeAt n m : ℝ) ^ (-(j : ℤ))`; N_j = n^d/p^j is real division (`Nj`), σ^{N_j} and σ^{N_1/p_i} are `Real.rpow`.

r_d(p,v) = `rdCoeff p v d` and [d 1]_{p_i} = `gaussBinom p_i d 1` use the q-Pascal recurrence; equality with the paper's product formula is the separately certified bridge `gaussBinomEqProdStatement`.
Standing hypotheses n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 2 of the appendix are explicit antecedents (n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1 are implied by 1 ≤ m < k, 1 ≤ j ≤ d anyway).

maps.label: Lemma A.1 = sandwich ∧ union bound

tex.text: Let $1\le m<k$ and $1\le j\le d$. Then

maps.note: The hypotheses and both displayed claims; the sandwich and the union bound are frozen separately and conjoined.

maps.label: 1 ≤ m < k
maps.note: Same range in both parts; k = ω(n) is `kOf n`.

maps.label: 1 ≤ j ≤ d
maps.note: Only the sandwich has j; the union bound is the j = 1 case, so it has no j binder.

maps.label: standing n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 2
maps.note: Not restated by the lemma: n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1 are the standing hypotheses of Definition 2.1, and the lemma sits in the proof of Theorem 6.1 (σ ≥ 2). In the sandwich, n ≥ 2 and d ≥ 1 also follow from 1 ≤ m < k and 1 ≤ j ≤ d; the union bound has no j and keeps d ≥ 1 explicitly. Per the Lean docstring both inequalities also hold for σ = 1 (checked), so σ ≥ 2 loses nothing.

maps.label: k = ω(n)
maps.note: Number of distinct prime factors.

maps.label: p_1 < ⋯ < p_k (0-indexed)
maps.note: `primeAt n i` is the (i+1)-st smallest prime factor; the default 0 is never reached under i < k.

maps.label: p := p_{m+1}
maps.note: 0-indexing: p_{m+1} = `primeAt n m`; it is inlined everywhere in the Lean statements.

maps.label: q^m(c) (truncation, scaled exponents)

lean.text:
∑ v ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m → Fin (d + 1))).erase 0,
    (-1 : ℝ) ^ (1 + ∑ i : Fin m, ((v i : Fin (d + 1)) : ℕ)) *
      (∏ i : Fin m, (rdCoeff (primeAt n i) ((v i : Fin (d + 1)) : ℕ) d : ℝ)) *
      (σ : ℝ) ^ (c * (n : ℝ) ^ d *
        ∏ i : Fin m, (primeAt n i : ℝ) ^ (-(((v i : Fin (d + 1)) : ℕ) : ℤ)))

maps.note: Literal transcription of the defining display, real-valued.

maps.label: v ∈ {0,…,d}^m, v ≠ 0
maps.note: Vectors as functions `Fin m → Fin (d+1)`; the zero vector is erased. Component i is the paper's v_{i+1}.

maps.label: (−1)^{1+|v|}
maps.note: |v| = Σ v_i.

maps.label: ∏ r_d(p_i, v_i)

lean.text: ∏ i : Fin m, (rdCoeff (primeAt n i) ((v i : Fin (d + 1)) : ℕ) d : ℝ)

maps.note: r_d(p,v) is `rdCoeff p v d` (ℕ), cast to ℝ.

maps.label: r_d(p,v) = p^{C(v,2)}[d v]_p
maps.note: Project definition (Statement.lean).

maps.label: Gaussian binomial: product formula vs q-Pascal

lean.text: | dd + 1, r + 1 => gaussBinom q dd r + q ^ (r + 1) * gaussBinom q dd (r + 1)
(gaussBinom q d r : ℝ) = gaussProd (q : ℝ) d r

maps.note: Lean defines [d r]_q by the q-Pascal recurrence; the bridge (certified) shows it equals the paper's product formula for every integer q ≥ 2.

maps.label: σ^{cN∏ p_i^{-v_i}}

lean.text:
(σ : ℝ) ^ (c * (n : ℝ) ^ d *
        ∏ i : Fin m, (primeAt n i : ℝ) ^ (-(((v i : Fin (d + 1)) : ℕ) : ℤ)))

maps.note: Real power with real exponent; N = n^d written out. Integrality of the exponent at c = p^{-j} is the separate claim `exponentIntegralityStatement` (proof of Lemma A.1).

maps.label: 0 ≤ q^m(p^{-j}) ≤ σ^{N_j}

lean.text:
0 ≤ qTrunc n d σ m ((primeAt n m : ℝ) ^ (-(j : ℤ))) ∧
      qTrunc n d σ m ((primeAt n m : ℝ) ^ (-(j : ℤ))) ≤ (σ : ℝ) ^ (Nj n d (primeAt n m) j)

maps.note: The chained inequality as a conjunction of two inequalities in ℝ.

maps.label: 0 ≤ q^m(p^{-j})

lean.text: 0 ≤ qTrunc n d σ m ((primeAt n m : ℝ) ^ (-(j : ℤ)))

maps.note: Nonnegativity.

maps.label: q^m(p^{-j})

lean.text: qTrunc n d σ m ((primeAt n m : ℝ) ^ (-(j : ℤ)))

maps.note: q^m evaluated at the scale c = p^{-j}.

maps.label: c = p^{-j}
maps.note: Integer power (zpow) in ℝ.

maps.label: q^m(p^{-j}) ≤ σ^{N_j}

lean.text: qTrunc n d σ m ((primeAt n m : ℝ) ^ (-(j : ℤ))) ≤ (σ : ℝ) ^ (Nj n d (primeAt n m) j)

maps.note: The trivial bound.

maps.label: σ^{N_j}

lean.text: (σ : ℝ) ^ (Nj n d (primeAt n m) j)

maps.note: `Real.rpow` with the real exponent N_j; it is an integer (p^j ∣ n^d), see the proof.

maps.label: N_j := n^d/p^j
maps.note: Real division, no truncation.

maps.label: q^m(p^{-1}) ≤ Σ_{i≤m} [d 1]_{p_i} σ^{N_1/p_i}

lean.text:
qTrunc n d σ m ((primeAt n m : ℝ) ^ (-(1 : ℤ))) ≤
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range m,
        (gaussBinom (primeAt n i) d 1 : ℝ) * (σ : ℝ) ^ (Nj n d (primeAt n m) 1 / (primeAt n i : ℝ))

maps.note: Inequality in ℝ.

maps.label: q^m(p^{-1})

lean.text: qTrunc n d σ m ((primeAt n m : ℝ) ^ (-(1 : ℤ)))

maps.note: p^{-1} as zpow (−1).

maps.label: Σ_{i ≤ m}
maps.note: 1-indexed i ≤ m ↔ 0-indexed i ∈ range m (`primeAt n i` = p_{i+1}).

maps.label: [d 1]_{p_i}
maps.note: q-Pascal Gaussian binomial (= product formula by the bridge), cast to ℝ.

maps.label: σ^{N_1/p_i}

lean.text: (σ : ℝ) ^ (Nj n d (primeAt n m) 1 / (primeAt n i : ℝ))

maps.note: Real power, real exponent N_1/p_i.
